messages.content: People are saying: RoboRide announces many/7 coverage, a few minute average wait, very cheap per mile. Autonomous delivery service. (You're not sure of the exact details.)
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Auto sector revenue index: 75 (baseline: 100). Foot traffic and sales are somewhat down.

Community action: Tamika Jefferson — follow up with the two business owners who sent dms after the linkedin post about foot-traffic patterns and roboride corridors. these are not cold leads — they engaged publicly and then reached out privately, which is the highest signal of interest short of an inbound inquiry. reply to both dms today with a specific, direct message: acknowledge what they asked, give a one-paragraph concrete answer that demonstrates real knowledge, then close with a single question — 'would it make sense to get on a 20-minute call this week to talk about how this applies to your specific situation?' no deck, no portfolio link, no pitch. one question. if they say yes, schedule the call for this week and be ready to send an agreement before it ends.

Community action: Kevin O'Brien — follow up with amir patel to confirm he has submitted the outstanding business cash flow documentation required for conditional loan approval. this loan is one piece of paperwork away from closing. a closed loan demonstrates origination capacity to sandra, generates fee income, and strengthens the portfolio expansion case whether the answer is yes or no. i contact amir by phone today, confirm the document status, and set a hard deadline of 48 hours for submission so we can move to final approval this week.
People around you are stressed: Angela Wright. The mood is tense.

You heard directly from Patricia Hawkins (CEO, Regional Auto Group): Conduct the market intelligence conversation with Stephanie Morris about commercial real estate conditions in Millfield — specifically lease termination flexibility, sublease market depth for automotive-zoned properties, and whether the closed location's lease has any assignment or buyout clause worth pursuing. The goal is to know whether the closed location is a sunk cost I hold until term or an obligation I can exit or monetize. This conversation was scheduled last tick. I am having it this week.

You heard directly from Patricia Hawkins (CEO, Regional Auto Group): Contact a business insurance broker — not AutoShield, not Linda Park, a third-party independent broker — and request a quote on a business owner's policy covering the three surviving locations. Also price personal disability insurance for myself. The current state.json shows 'none' for insurance coverage, and I have three dependents. A single liability event against an uninsured business in a year when my savings are already declining is the kind of risk that does not announce itself before it arrives.

You heard directly from Patricia Hawkins (CEO, Regional Auto Group): Call David Chen at First Community Bank — not to ask for anything, but to give him a structured update on Regional Auto Group's financial position and consolidation plan. Three locations, reduced debt load from the closure, EV certification investment, community partnership with the Millfield Auto Tech Pipeline. Frame this as a relationship maintenance call from a long-term business account holder who wants the bank to understand the restructuring before it shows up as a credit question. The goal is to raise his trust level before I need him, not after.

Objective: understand their workforce transition challenges, establish whether AV/automation disruption is creating HR needs in their sector, and position Wright Workforce Advisory LLC as a methodological resource — not a vendor pitch, but a genuine professional conversation that ends with a next step. Walk away with either a clear 'not now' or a concrete follow-up action. Document the call in Wright Workforce Advisory LLC's CRM log.

You heard directly from Jake Morrison (Car Salesperson): Call Rick Tanner directly — not email, a phone call — and tell him the two weeks he mentioned are almost up and I am still holding. I am not pressuring him, I am making myself easy to say yes to. I say: 'Rick, you told me two weeks. I wanted you to know I have not taken anything else and I am ready for that conversation whenever you are.' I keep it short. I let him respond. If he has an answer, I am ready to move. If he needs more time, I note the date and give him a hard follow-up window in my own head.
